# Downtime dispatcher should dispatch into project workspace (WL-0MU321YK70035AYT)

**Headline**: Change the herdr downtime dispatcher so that an automated pane for a work item written in project `R` spawns in the herdr workspace that hosts the herdr plugin (worklist) pane for `R`, inside a tab named after the work item ID (created on first use, reused thereafter), instead of the machine-wide `Dispatcher` workspace and its per-prefix tabs. If no plugin pane for `R` can be resolved, fall back to the existing `Dispatcher` workspace anchor.

## Problem statement

Automated downtime dispatches currently spawn into a dedicated machine-wide `Dispatcher` workspace — anchored by a persisted anchor pane (`~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-dispatch-anchor.json`) and, after C1, routed by work-item prefix into per-prefix tabs inside that workspace (`downtime-dispatch-tab-anchors.json`). The producer rejected per-project tabs ("We are not getting per project tabs", audit on WL-0MTRQT482001SNXC). The desired behaviour is that dispatched panes land in the project's own herdr workspace — in a tab named after the work item — so automated work is co-located with the project it belongs to and each work item has its own reusable tab.

## Users

- **Herdr operator running 2+ project workspaces** (e.g. ContextHub `WL`, Tableau Card Engine `CG`, AI Hell `AH`, SorraAgents `SA`):
  > "As an operator, I want automated downtime panes for project `X` to appear in project `X`'s herdr workspace under a tab named after the work item, so I can watch a specific item's dispatch and context without leaving the project."
- **Overnight / on-call dispatch reviewer**:
  > "As an on-call engineer, I want each project's automated panes to sit with that project's workspace, grouped per work item in its own tab, so a project's overnight activity is visible in context and never intermixed with another project's."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Project-workspace placement** — for an automated dispatch of work item `<PREFIX>-<hash>` whose worklog root is `R`, the spawned `Downtime triggered …` pane's `workspace_id` equals the herdr workspace that hosts the herdr plugin/worklist pane (`label == "Work Items"`) whose logical project root is `R`; verified with `herdr pane list` (new pane's `workspace_id`) and `herdr tab list` (the plugin pane's workspace). No dispatched pane for root `R` lands in the `Dispatcher` workspace (except via the fallback in AC4) or in another project's workspace.
2. **Per-work-item tab placement** — within the target workspace, the dispatcher ensures a tab whose label is exactly the work item ID exists (`herdr tab create --workspace <workspaceId> --label <itemId> --no-focus` when absent) and reuses the existing tab when one with that exact label already exists; it then spawns the pane inside that tab by splitting the tab's anchor (root) pane (`send-to-pi.sh --anchor <tabRootPaneId>`), so a second dispatch for the same item adds a pane to the same tab rather than creating a duplicate tab. Verified via `herdr tab list` (`label == <itemId>` in the workspace) and `herdr pane list` (new pane's `tab_id` equals that tab's `tab_id`).
3. **Deterministic project→workspace resolution** — resolution matches the candidate's `worklogRoot` against the plugin pane's logical project root (`HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD`, readable via `herdr pane process-info --pane <id>` + `/proc/<shell_pid>/environ`), not against pane `cwd` (which for plugin panes is the plugin directory) and not against the workspace label. Resolution is fail-closed on ambiguity/failure and never selects another project's workspace.
4. **Fallback when no plugin pane exists** — if no live plugin pane for `R` can be resolved, the dispatcher falls back to the existing machine-wide `Dispatcher` workspace anchor (`getDispatcherAnchor`, `downtime-dispatch-anchor.json`), which is retained for exactly this case; panes spawned via the fallback may use the `Dispatcher` workspace (per-prefix tab routing is still retired). Never falls back to the leader's current pane.
5. **Rejected C1 per-prefix routing retired** — prefix-based routing (`candidate.id.split('-')[0]` tab labels, `downtime-dispatch-tab-anchors.json`) is removed from the worklog dispatch path; the tab-provisioning machinery is repurposed to key tabs by full work-item ID (AC2) in the resolved project workspace. The `Dispatcher` anchor file/provisioning is retained only for the AC4 fallback.
6. **No regression to dispatch correctness** — selection/ranking (Herdr list head), coordination, round-robin, CAS claim (`--if-status/--if-stage`), staged-marker exclusion, `code-freeze` and `needsProducerReview` gates, per-item `cwd` forwarding, pane naming, and the dispatch audit log (`.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`, `downtime-log.ts` kinds) remain unchanged.
7. **Tests** — unit/integration coverage for: project workspace resolution (root → plugin workspace), per-item tab create-or-reuse (first dispatch creates, second reuses), no-plugin-pane fallback to the Dispatcher anchor, multiple-plugin-pane handling, malformed `herdr pane list`/`tab list`/`process-info` output (fail-closed), anchor forwarding to `send-to-pi.sh --anchor`, and removal of per-prefix routing; all existing `packages/herdr` tests adjusted and green.
8. **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.**
9. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- Automated downtime dispatch only (`dispatchClaimedTier` / `dispatchFromCoordination`); manual `open-worklist` / `open-pi-agent` flows keep current behaviour.
- Reuse the existing spawn surface: `send-to-pi.sh --anchor <paneId>` (`pane split --pane`) and `grid.py`; do not invent a new pane-creation mechanism.
- Reuse existing fail-closed conventions (no pane, no marker on an unresolvable target) — an unresolved workspace or tab must never fall back to the wrong project.
- Tab provisioning must tolerate herdr CLI output-shape drift (`tab_id`/`tabId`/`id`, nested `result`, `pane_id`/`paneId`) and log raw output on parse failure (existing convention).
- The coordination lock (`tryAcquireCoordLock`) guards tab creation if concurrent creates for the same item/workspace are possible; no new lock mechanism.
- Scheduled prompts have no work-item ID; they keep the `Dispatcher` anchor path (see Risks/assumptions).

## Existing state

- **C0 (WL-0MTR01EU7005SYZG, completed)** added `dispatcher-anchor.ts`: `getDispatcherAnchor()` provisions one `Dispatcher` workspace + anchor pane, persisted to `~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-dispatch-anchor.json`, and `dispatchClaimedTier` forwards its pane id as `anchorId`.
- **C1 (WL-0MTRQT482001SNXC, open, audit rejected "We are not getting per project tabs.")** added `getDispatcherTabAnchor()`: routes `<PREFIX>` (`candidate.id.split('-', 1)[0]`) to a tab labelled with the prefix inside the `Dispatcher` workspace, persisted to `~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-dispatch-tab-anchors.json`. Live state today: `Dispatcher` workspace `w34` holds prefix tabs `WL`, `AH`, `SA`, `CG`, `OSL`; the live anchor file points at `w36:p1`.
- **Existing tab machinery is largely reusable**: `getDispatcherTabAnchor` already implements find-tab-by-label → adopt-with-live-pane → else create, under the coordination lock, with CLI-shape tolerance and fail-closed parsing (`packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.ts`). This item re-targets it to an arbitrary workspace keyed by the full work-item ID.
- **Live evidence for the target mapping** (this host): each project workspace hosts a plugin pane with `label == "Work Items"`; `herdr pane process-info --pane w2V:pB` → `shell_pid` whose `/proc/<pid>/environ` carries `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD=/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub` and `HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID=w2V`. Similarly `w2Y:pW` → `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD=/home/rgardler/projects/Tableau-Card-Engine`, `HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID=w2Y`. The plugin pane's reported `cwd` is the plugin directory (`/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/packages/herdr`), so resolution must use `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD`, not `cwd`.
- **Duplicate item** `WL-0MU7JZE04008VKP0` was closed as a duplicate (producer Q1); this item is canonical.

## Desired change

1. Add a project-workspace resolver (in `dispatcher-anchor.ts` or a sibling module) that, given a worklog root `R`, returns the herdr plugin pane/workspace for `R` (`{ paneId, workspaceId, tabId } | null`) by enumerating `herdr pane list`, filtering plugin panes (`label == "Work Items"`), reading each plugin pane's `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD` via `herdr pane process-info` + `/proc/<shell_pid>/environ`, and matching `R`.
2. Add/extend a tab anchor resolver that, given `workspaceId` and a tab label (the work item ID), returns the tab's anchor pane: fast-path an existing tab with that exact label (adopting its live root pane), else `herdr tab create --workspace <workspaceId> --label <itemId> --no-focus` (under the coordination lock with a double-check); fail-closed `null` on any parse/CLI failure.
3. Wire the worklog dispatch path (`dispatchClaimedTier`) to: resolve the project workspace (AC1/AC3) → ensure/reuse the item-ID tab (AC2) → forward the tab's anchor pane as `anchorId` to `spawnAgentPane` → `send-to-pi.sh --anchor <paneId>`. When the project workspace cannot be resolved, fall back to `getDispatcherAnchor` (AC4).
4. Retire per-prefix routing and the per-prefix persistence file from the worklog path; keep `getDispatcherAnchor` and its file for the fallback.
5. Add tests and update `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` and `packages/herdr/README.md` accordingly.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.ts` — new project-workspace/plugin-pane resolver (`herdr pane list` + `pane process-info` + `/proc` env read); repurpose `getDispatcherTabAnchor` to workspace + item-ID label; retire prefix semantics and `downtime-dispatch-tab-anchors.json`.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `dispatchClaimedTier` anchor resolution (project workspace → item-ID tab, fallback to `getDispatcherAnchor`); dep type changes; scheduled-prompt path unchanged (Dispatcher anchor).
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `createDowntimeDeps` / `defaultDispatcherAnchorResolver` / `defaultDispatcherTabAnchorResolver` wiring; new/changed resolver deps.
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/coordination-dispatch.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts` — resolution + create-or-reuse tab + fallback tests; remove per-prefix tests.
- `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh` / `packages/herdr/shared/grid.py` — no behavioural change expected (anchor is any pane id); verify.
- `~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-dispatch-anchor.json` (retained for fallback) / `downtime-dispatch-tab-anchors.json` (retired).
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `packages/herdr/README.md` — replace the C0/C1 placement sections with the project-workspace + item-ID-tab invariant.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: no plugin pane open for a project** → fall back to the `Dispatcher` anchor (producer Q2 answer (b)) — deliberately never the leader's pane, so placement stays neutral rather than wrong-project.
- **Risk: multiple plugin panes for one root** (operator opened several `Worklog` tabs across workspaces) → ambiguous target. Assumption: choose deterministically (e.g. the focused/first matching pane by pane id); confirm during implementation.
- **Risk: tab-label collision with a user-created tab** — an operator tab already named exactly `<itemId>` in the project workspace is reused (per Q3), which is the intended behaviour but means the dispatcher may add a pane to an operator's tab; `--no-focus` prevents focus stealing.
- **Risk: `/proc` env read is Linux-specific and requires the shell_pid from `pane process-info`.** This is the same mechanism already used by `packages/herdr/scripts/open.sh`; acceptable on this host (Linux). Non-Linux degradation → fall back per AC4 or fail-closed.
- **Risk: tab create/reuse races** — two dispatches for the same new item ID could both create the tab. `tryAcquireCoordLock` + double-check inside the lock, plus the existing "adopt an existing matching tab" path, mitigate this (existing C1 pattern).
- **Scope-creep guard:** out of scope — changing selection/ranking, the audit freshness gate, the coordination/leader model, or manual pane flows; "dispatcher workspace has useless pane" (WL-0MU2EOHK900425VU) and leftover `Dispatcher` workspace cleanup stay separate.
- **Assumption:** plugin panes are identifiable by `label == "Work Items"` and carry `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD` + `HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID` in the shell process environment.
- **Assumption:** scheduled prompts (no work-item ID) keep using the `Dispatcher` anchor path; if the producer wants them resolved into the project workspace, that is a follow-up.
- **Assumption:** the item-ID tab is created in the resolved project workspace only; the AC4 Dispatcher fallback uses the existing single anchor pane (no item-ID tab), since Q2 named "the existing `Dispatcher` workspace anchor".

## Related work

- **WL-0MU7JZE04008VKP0 — "Dispatched panes should go under the project workspace"** (closed as a duplicate; producer resolved Q1 in favour of this item) — the same intent ("spawned in the same tab as the herdr extension for that project"). This item is now the canonical work item.
- **WL-0MTR01EU7005SYZG — "Downtime dispatch panes all spawn in the leader's workspace regardless of project (C0: anchor-by-ID into dedicated Dispatcher workspace)"** (completed) — the C0 design this item reverses for the primary path; children `WL-0MTR2CD4X006XI7U`, `WL-0MTR2HLLJ009PTPJ`, `WL-0MTR2JOTE006T3XT`.
- **WL-0MTRQT482001SNXC — "Downtime dispatcher: per-project tabs in Dispatcher workspace"** (open, `plan_complete`, audit rejected) — the C1 per-prefix tab work this item retires; rejected by producer with "We are not getting per project tabs."
- **WL-0MTRBOU0Y002M2CX — "Downtime dispatches land in Podcast workspace instead of Dispatcher workspace"** (completed) — the incident that motivated the Dispatcher anchor; context for why placement was moved out of project workspaces, now being moved back deliberately.
- **WL-0MU2EOHK900425VU — "dispatcher workspace has useless pane"** (open, `intake_complete`) — adjacent cleanup of the `Dispatcher` workspace.
- **WL-0MU2LF6SZ000JQYI / WL-0MU2LFHBH004VF48** (completed) — C1 per-prefix anchor provisioning and docs/integration tests whose machinery is repurposed here.
- **`packages/herdr/scripts/open.sh`** — prior art for reading `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD` from a plugin pane's shell process (the resolution mechanism this item needs).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MTR01EU7005SYZG** – Downtime dispatch panes all spawn in the leader's workspace regardless of project (C0: anchor-by-ID into dedicated Dispatcher workspace) (completed)
- **WL-0MLSHA2FE0T8RR8X** – Implement multi-directory plugin discovery with precedence (completed)
- **WL-0MS6LS2TF007AV63** – Implement tab working directory support in herdr plugin (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: acceptable, acceptance, activity, add, added (+286 more)
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: 0mtr01eu7005syzg, 0mtrqt482001snxc, add, added, agent (+279 more)
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: 0mtr01eu7005syzg, activity, add, added, agent (+215 more)

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-09-28T07:30:08Z — `/skill:plan` (session `herdr-1790579668-240852-24530`): approved 5-feature test-first plan; created children F1 `WL-0MUKXFV4O006G8HZ`, F2 `WL-0MUKXFVMS001BP68`, F3 `WL-0MUKXFW3N003RZSK`, F4 `WL-0MUKXFWLD006A8XI`, F5 `WL-0MUKXFX2M0019E3G`; wired dependencies F1→F2→F3→F4→F5; recorded Appendix Q4–Q6 (operator accepted recommended options (a)/(a)/(a)); six review stages + AC coverage review (100%, proceed).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

### Q1 — duplicate item reconciliation (RESOLVED)

- Q: "`WL-0MU7JZE04008VKP0` ("Dispatched panes should go under the project workspace", open/`idea`/high) describes the same change — "spawned in the same tab as the herdr extension for that project". Both items cannot be implemented independently. How should we reconcile them? Options: (a) keep `WL-0MU321YK70035AYT` as canonical and close `WL-0MU7JZE04008VKP0` as a duplicate; (b) keep `WL-0MU7JZE04008VKP0` as canonical and close this item as a duplicate; (c) make one a child of the other; (d) implement both separately." — **Answer (producer): (a) keep `WL-0MU321YK70035AYT` as canonical; close `WL-0MU7JZE04008VKP0` as a duplicate.** Source: interactive reply. Action taken: `wl close WL-0MU7JZE04008VKP0 --reason "Duplicate of WL-0MU321YK70035AYT …"` (closed successfully). This item is the canonical work item.

### Q2 — fallback when no plugin pane exists for the item's project (RESOLVED)

- Q: "When a dispatch candidate belongs to worklog root `R` but no live herdr plugin pane for `R` can be resolved, what should the dispatcher do? Options: (a) fail-closed — no dispatch this cycle; (b) fall back to the existing `Dispatcher` workspace anchor (retain `downtime-dispatch-anchor.json` for this case only); (c) fall back to the leader's current pane; (d) skip the candidate and continue to the next." — **Answer (producer): (b) fall back to the existing `Dispatcher` workspace anchor.** Source: interactive reply. Implication: `getDispatcherAnchor` and `downtime-dispatch-anchor.json` are retained for the fallback case only; (a)/(c)/(d) not chosen; per-prefix routing is still retired.

### Q3 — placement within the project workspace (RESOLVED)

- Q: "Within the target project workspace, where should the dispatched pane be placed? Options: (a) split the project's plugin/worklist pane (same tab as the Worklog pane); (b) open a new tab in the project workspace; (c) split the project's terminal pane; (d) provision a dedicated anchor pane per project workspace." — **Answer (producer): open a tab named after the work item ID; if a tab with that ID already exists, reuse it and add a new pane to that tab.** Source: interactive reply. Implication: implement a create-or-reuse tab keyed by the full work item ID in the resolved project workspace; the pane is added by splitting that tab's anchor pane.

### Q4 — ambiguity when multiple plugin panes resolve to the same root (RESOLVED)

- Q: "When two or more live herdr plugin (`Work Items`) panes resolve to the same logical project root `R` (an operator anomaly), how should the dispatcher choose the target workspace/tab? Options: (a) prefer the focused matching pane, else the lowest pane id (deterministic); (b) lowest pane id only (ignore focus); (c) treat as unresolved → fall back to the `Dispatcher` anchor (AC4); (d) fail-closed — no dispatch this cycle, no marker." — **Answer (producer): accepted the plan as presented, including the recommended option (a) — prefer the focused matching pane, else the lowest pane id.** Source: interactive reply ("LGTM"). Implication: AC3 ambiguity resolution is deterministic and always lands inside a workspace that genuinely hosts `R`.

### Q5 — per-item tab on the AC4 fallback (RESOLVED)

- Q: "On the AC4 fallback (no resolvable plugin pane for `R`), should the pane still get a per-item tab? Options: (a) use the existing single `Dispatcher` anchor pane as-is (no item-ID tab); (b) create/reuse an item-ID tab inside the `Dispatcher` workspace, mirroring AC2." — **Answer (producer): accepted the plan as presented, including the recommended option (a) — existing single `Dispatcher` anchor pane, no item-ID tab.** Source: interactive reply ("LGTM"). Implication: the fallback path stays as C0; only the primary path gains item-ID tabs.

### Q6 — scheduled prompts (RESOLVED)

- Q: "Scheduled prompts have a project root (`opts.cwd`) but no work-item ID. Should they keep the `Dispatcher` anchor (current) or also route into the project workspace? Options: (a) keep the `Dispatcher` anchor (out of scope for this item); (b) route into the project workspace with a non-item tab label; (c) route into the project workspace reusing a single `Scheduled` tab." — **Answer (producer): accepted the plan as presented, including the recommended option (a) — keep the `Dispatcher` anchor; a follow-up item can revisit.** Source: interactive reply ("LGTM"). Implication: `dispatchScheduledPrompt` is unchanged.

### Resolved by research (not producer questions)

- Q: "How is 'the herdr plugin for project R' identified?" — Answer (research): the herdr plugin pane has `label == "Work Items"` (the plugin pane entrypoint title, from `herdr-plugin.toml`), and its shell process environment carries `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD=<project root>` and `HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID=<workspace id>` (verified live: `w2V:pB` → `ContextHub`/`w2V`; `w2Y:pW` → `Tableau-Card-Engine`/`w2Y`). The pane's reported `cwd` is the plugin directory, so resolution must read `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD` via `herdr pane process-info` + `/proc/<shell_pid>/environ` (same technique already used by `packages/herdr/scripts/open.sh`). Evidence: live `herdr pane list` / `pane process-info` on this host.
- Q: "Do scheduled prompts have a project root to resolve?" — Answer (research): yes — `dispatchScheduledPrompt` receives `opts.cwd` = the project's worklog root (per-root `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`); however they have no work-item ID, so they keep the `Dispatcher` anchor path (see assumption).
- Q: "What does the existing C0/C1 state look like?" — Answer (research): `~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-dispatch-tab-anchors.json` maps `w34` → prefixes `WL`/`AH`/`SA`/`CG`/`OSL`; `downtime-dispatch-anchor.json` points at `w36:p1`. Evidence: live files on this host.
- Q: "Is the existing tab machinery reusable for item-ID tabs?" — Answer (research): yes — `getDispatcherTabAnchor` already implements find-by-label → adopt-live-pane → create under the coordination lock with CLI-shape tolerance; it needs workspace + label parameterisation rather than a rewrite. Evidence: `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.ts`.

# Intake Brief — wl sync to be run before refactor and standup skills (WL-0MUAD8U24001ZK5K)

## Problem statement

The `refactor` and `standup` skills read and (for refactor) create worklog data, but neither begins by pulling remote worklog changes. A stale local SQLite store can therefore produce duplicate `REFACTOR` work items, stale standup reports, and un-pushed local changes. The requested behaviour is that **`wl sync` runs as the first action** of both skills, before any other worklog interaction.

## Users

- **Agents invoking `/skill:refactor` or `/skill:standup`** — they need current worklog data so analysis and reporting are based on the same state the operator sees.
  - *As an agent, I want refactor/standup to sync first, so I never file duplicate smells or report stale items.*
- **Operators reading standup reports** — the report must reflect the actual remote queue.
  - *As an operator, I want my standup to reflect synced data, so it drives the right priorities.*
- **Producers reviewing refactor-filed work items** — fewer duplicate `REFACTOR` items to triage.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `/skill:refactor` (both the no-ID full-project scan and the `<id>` session-only mode) performs `wl sync` as the **first worklog operation**, before any work-item read, comment injection, or work-item creation. Verified by an automated test asserting call ordering.
2. `/skill:standup` performs `wl sync` before its first `wl next` / `wl list` fetch. Verified by an automated test asserting call ordering.
3. The sync invocation is **lock-aware** (uses `wl sync --if-idle`) and single-flight, so overlapping or concurrent invocations skip rather than block or pile up. Verified by a test asserting the `--if-idle` argument / skip behaviour.
4. A **failed sync is non-fatal**: offline, unborn-HEAD, author-gate, or lock-contention failures log a warning and the skill continues with local data, preserving its existing exit-code semantics. Verified by a test that stubs a failing sync and asserts the skill still proceeds.
5. Both `SKILL.md` files document that `wl sync` runs first, what happens on failure, and how to disable it for offline/deterministic runs (`--no-sync`).
6. A `--no-sync` escape hatch (or equivalent injectable runner) exists so tests and offline runs never perform a real network sync; the existing test suites remain hermetic.
7. When no `.worklog` context is resolvable, sync is skipped gracefully rather than erroring.
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
9. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Target repository:** the `refactor` and `standup` skills are maintained in the **SorraAgents agent-framework repo** (`/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/skill/...`). This work item is tracked in the **ContextHub** worklog; see Open Questions — implementation location must be confirmed before the implement workflow can run.
- Sync must be bounded and non-interactive; it must never hang an agent session.
- No new third-party dependencies.
- Reuse the existing `wl` CLI and the shared `run_wl` helper (`skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py`) rather than shelling out ad hoc; a single shared helper should serve both skills to avoid divergence.
- Must not change refactor scan/detection semantics or standup report content/format.
- Respect repo ignore rules and the author-gate behaviour of `wl sync` (do not add `--allow-foreign-author`).

## Existing state

- **No skill currently runs `wl sync`.** A search of `skill/**/scripts/*.py` for sync calls returns none (only the `wl` CLI itself and the ContextHub herdr auto-sync).
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` exposes `run_wl(cmd)`, which injects `--worklog-dir` with prefix/cwd resolution — the natural wrapper for a shared `sync_worklog()` helper.
- `wl sync` supports `--if-idle` ("Skip (exit 0) if another sync is already in progress — lock-aware guard for auto-sync spawners"), `--no-push`, `--worklog-dir`, and `--json`.
- ContextHub's `packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.ts` already implements the `--if-idle` fire-and-forget pattern (single-flight guard + heartbeat freshness) — a proven precedent for non-blocking, non-fatal sync.
- `refactor.py` entry point: `main()` → `_build_pipeline_runner()` → pipeline; session mode wraps `StatusLifecycle(restore_on_exit=True)`.
- `generate_standup.py` entry point: `main()` resolves `--worklog-dir` then calls `generate_report()` which performs the `wl next` / `wl list` fetches via `fetch_json`.
- Existing tests: `skill/standup/tests/` (3 files: default output path, worklog-dir, regressions). Refactor has no dedicated test package in the skill tree.

## Desired change

1. Add a shared helper (e.g. `skill/shared/worklog_sync.py`) that runs `wl sync --if-idle` via `run_wl`, returns success/skip status, and never raises on failure.
2. Invoke it as the first action in both `refactor.py` and `generate_standup.py`, before any other `wl` call.
3. Add `--no-sync` to both scripts and thread it through so tests/offline runs skip syncing.
4. Update both `SKILL.md` files to state sync-first behaviour and the `--no-sync` flag.
5. Add focused tests for ordering, `--if-idle`, failure tolerance, and `--no-sync`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/skill/refactor/scripts/refactor.py` — invoke shared sync-first helper before the pipeline in `main()`.
- `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/skill/standup/scripts/generate_standup.py` — invoke shared sync-first helper in `main()` before `generate_report()`.
- `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/skill/shared/worklog_sync.py` — **new** shared helper wrapping `wl sync --if-idle` via `run_wl` (fail-soft).

# Gate leak: completed/in_review items with no audit (flag + doctor report)

## Problem statement

Work items can reach `completed`/`in_review` — and ship — with **no audit record at all**, and the no-audit population is invisible: 12 of 52 `completed`/`in_review` items had no audit, including the root-level `WL-0MU9Z7L8X00117BI` (Client retry does not honour Retry-After), advanced to `completed`/`in_review` and shipped (`5ccc2ae3`) without one. `closeDescendants` (`src/commands/close.ts`) closes every descendant via `closeSingle` without requiring a child audit, and nothing prevents a `status: completed` + `stage: in_review` transition without an audit. The gap must be made **visible** (report) and **guarded** (flag at closure/advance), with an explicit, recorded escape hatch (waiver).

## Users and user stories

- **Producer reviewing the release queue** — As a producer, I want `wl doctor` to list every `completed`/`in_review` item with no audit (with parent/child relationship and age), so the gap cannot silently accumulate and I can decide to audit or waive each one.
- **Release/automation operator** — As an operator, I want closing an unaudited root item to emit a clear, non-fatal warning, so I notice the gap at closure time without breaking existing automation or forcing `--force` for every legacy item.
- **Agent implementing/reviewing a sub-tree** — As an agent, I want a child closed under a fresh-audited parent to be treated as *covered* (derived, per the P6 child-coverage decision) and **not** flagged, so the report reflects reality and does not re-open already-covered work.
- **Developer handling a legitimate exception** — As a developer, I want to record an explicit waiver with a reason, so a deliberate audit exception is auditable rather than silent.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Explicit, durable waiver mechanism.** A `wl` command records an explicit waiver on a work item (recommended surface: `wl audit-waive <id> --reason "<text>" [--author <name>]` and `wl audit-unwaive <id>`), stored durably and machine-readable and surfaced in `wl show --json`. Verification: a test proves waive creates the record and unwaive removes it; the record is round-tripped through sync/JSONL.
2. **Closure/advance guard flags `completed`/`in_review` without a fresh audit (flag, not hard block).** When the non-force close/advance path closes a **root** item whose audit is absent or stale per the shared `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt, storedFingerprint, currentFingerprint)` predicate, and no waiver is recorded, the CLI emits a clear non-fatal warning naming the gap. `wl close --force` remains the explicit escape hatch (bypasses and records the bypass as a waiver/reason). Verification: closing an unaudited root item emits the warning; closing a root with a fresh audit or a waiver does not.
3. **Child coverage is honoured (derived, per `WL-0MUBVH8QG0020H9L`).** In both the close path and the report, a child (`parentId` set) is *covered* iff its **direct** parent has a fresh audit (reuse `isCoveredByParent`/`isAuditFresh` from `packages/shared/src/icons.ts`) — a covered child is not flagged; a child with no fresh parent audit is flagged unless waived. Coverage stays **derived at read time; nothing is persisted** (no schema migration for coverage). Verification: test — child under a fresh-audited parent is not flagged; child under a stale/unaudited parent is flagged; waived child is not flagged.
4. **`wl doctor` report of the no-audit population.** A read-only report (recommended: `wl doctor audit-gaps [--json]`, no `--apply`) lists every `completed`/`in_review` item with **no audit record**, showing for each: root vs `child of <parent-id>`, age (derived from `updatedAt`/`activityAt`), and coverage/waiver status (covered / uncovered / waived). Verification: a CLI/integration test against a fixture DB asserts the reported rows and fields, and that covered/waived items are excluded from the flagged set (or shown as covered/waived).
5. **Tests and documentation.** Tests cover all three required scenarios from the description — root item advanced without audit is flagged; child under an audited parent is not flagged; a waiver suppresses the flag — plus report field content. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `README`, CLI help text, and any relevant docs-site entries. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Reuse, do not fork, the freshness predicate.** `isAuditFresh` in `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` is the single source of truth for "fresh audit" (WL-0MSIAOFI70075REE, WL-0MUBVH7ZR009PP80, WL-0MUBVH5S0008NQ9K). The guard/report must call it — no competing `auditedAt`-vs-`updatedAt` comparison.
- **Non-fatal guard.** The closure guard must not break existing automation; it warns/flags. A hard block was explicitly avoided (see Assumptions).
- **Derived coverage, no coverage persistence.** Per WL-0MUBVH8QG0020H9L, child coverage is derived at read time; do not add a persisted coverage reference or coverage-specific migration.
- **Migrations are review-gated.** Any new column (only the waiver record, if a DB-backed design is chosen) must go through `src/migrations/` and `wl doctor upgrade`, never a silent ALTER.
- **CLI and herdr agree.** Where the no-audit/covered notion is consumed by both the CLI and the herdr display/dispatch paths, keep the predicate in `@worklog/shared` (single source of truth).
- **Scope discipline.** This item owns *reporting and flagging* the gate leak; it must not re-open the P6 display work or the root-only dispatch decision (WL-0MSTLFW14000KPEC).

## Existing state

- `src/commands/close.ts` — `closeSingle()` sets `status: completed` / `stage: done` with no audit check; `closeDescendants()` closes the whole subtree via `closeSingle()`. The recursive path only requires the **parent** to be `in_review` with `auditResult.readyToClose === true`; `--force` bypasses all checks.
- `src/commands/doctor.ts` — `doctor stage-sync` already detects stale status/stage combinations (with `--apply`), but has no audit rule/report. `doctor` also has `prune`, `foreign-items`, `priority`, `file-paths`, `migrate`.
- `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` — `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt, storedFingerprint?, currentFingerprint?)` (content-fingerprint primary, legacy 60 s time floor fallback) and `isCoveredByParent(item, parentAudit)` (derived depth-1 child coverage) already exist.
- `src/persistent-store.ts` — `audit_results` table (latest-only, sole source of truth for audit state); `workitems` has no waiver/coverage column. `src/migrations/index.ts` has the fingerprint migration precedent.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` documents derived child coverage and root-only audit dispatch.
- No `waiver` concept exists anywhere in `src/`, `packages/`, or `docs/`.

## Desired change

1. Introduce an **explicit, durable waiver** for the no-audit gate (recommended: `wl audit-waive` / `wl audit-unwaive`, backed by a nullable waiver record) — the only permitted schema addition in this item.
2. Add a shared **audit-gap predicate** that classifies an item as `covered` (child under fresh-audited direct parent), `waived`, or `uncovered`/`no-audit`, reusing `isAuditFresh`/`isCoveredByParent`.
3. Wire a **non-fatal closure guard** so the non-force close/advance path warns when a root item is closed without a fresh audit and without a waiver; keep `--force` as the explicit bypass.
4. Add a read-only **`wl doctor` report** listing `completed`/`in_review` no-audit items with root/child relationship, age, and coverage/waiver status.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/commands/doctor.ts` — New read-only `audit-gaps` subcommand (report), following the existing `foreign-items` report/`--json` pattern.
- `src/commands/close.ts` — Non-fatal warning in `closeSingle`/recursive/standard paths; honour derived child coverage and waivers.
- `src/commands/audit.ts` (or new `src/commands/audit-waive.ts`) — `wl audit-waive` / `wl audit-unwaive` commands.
- `src/persistent-store.ts` — Waiver record read/write (and nullable column in the `workitems` CREATE TABLE for new DBs).
- `src/migrations/index.ts` — Migration adding the nullable waiver column (review-gated via `wl doctor upgrade`).
- `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` — Extend the shared coverage helpers with the `covered`/`waived`/`uncovered` classification reused by CLI and herdr.
- `src/commands/helpers.ts` / `src/commands/show.ts` — Surface the waiver in `wl show --json`.
- `tests/` — New tests for the guard, the report, coverage/waiver suppression, and the migration.

## Design decisions & assumptions

> These are agent-adopted decisions, recorded per the global "reasonable assumptions must be documented" rule. They are low-risk implementation choices within a clear requirement and are surfaced for producer review; a producer may override at review/plan time.

- **Flag, not hard block (AC2).** The title ("flag + doctor report"), AC1's "flags or blocks", and WL-0MUBVH8QG0020H9L's explicit assignment of "durable uncovered-child reporting" to this item indicate a reporting/warning guard, not a hard gate. Hard-blocking close/advance would break existing automation and force `--force` for every legacy item, so the guard warns and the report enumerates.
- **Waiver storage = nullable record, not a comment marker.** A durable, machine-readable record (persisted and surfaced in `wl show --json`) is preferred over a parsed comment, because audit comments are deprecated/non-canonical and a waiver must be queryable by the report and syncable. This is the only schema change in scope.
- **Report scope = no-audit items (AC4), coverage-aware.** The report enumerates items with **no audit record** (the accumulation problem from the description). It distinguishes covered (header/child under fresh-audited parent), waived, and genuinely uncovered. Stale-but-present audits are handled by the guard (AC2) and by the existing freshness/icon surfaces, not duplicated here.
- **Command naming.** `wl doctor audit-gaps` and `wl audit-waive`/`wl audit-unwaive` are recommended names; a reviewer/planner may rename without changing intent.
- **`--force` as waiver.** `wl close --force` already exists as the documented bypass of audit/stage checks; it is treated as an explicit waiver and (recommended) records a waiver/reason so the bypass is auditable.

## Risks and mitigations

- **Scope creep into P6 display work.** Mitigation: this item changes only the report/guard and the derived classification helper; it must not alter icon rendering or relax root-only dispatch (WL-0MSTLFW14000KPEC).
- **Waiver mechanism adds a migration.** Mitigation: it is the only schema change; it is nullable, review-gated via `src/migrations/`, and old rows default to "no waiver" (fail-safe: absence never suppresses a flag).
- **False "covered" suppression.** Mitigation: coverage is depth-1 only and requires a *fresh* direct-parent audit via the shared `isAuditFresh` predicate; a missing/stale parent audit leaves the child flagged.
- **Noise in the report for legacy items.** Mitigation: the report is read-only (no `--apply`) and lists with age/relationship so operators can bulk-waive or audit deliberately rather than being forced to act.
- **Scope-creep risk (explicit).** Additional opportunities (e.g. auto-audit dispatch, hard gating, bulk waiver) are out of scope and must be captured as linked work items, not absorbed here.
- **Assumption risk.** The flag-vs-block and waiver-storage decisions are agent-adopted; if a producer prefers a hard block or a comment-marker waiver, the ACs and Key Files change. Flagged for producer review.

## Related work

- `WL-0MSIAOFI70075REE` — Unify audit-freshness at-or-near logic across icon display and downtime dispatcher (completed). Source of the shared freshness predicate; `discovered-from` of this item.
- `WL-0MUBVH8QG0020H9L` — Explicit child-audit coverage so covered children are not re-dispatched (completed). Decided coverage is **derived at read time, not persisted**, and explicitly assigned **durable uncovered-child reporting** to this item.
- `WL-0MUBVH5S0008NQ9K` — Audit freshness: content-fingerprint gate as primary (completed). The `isAuditFresh` fingerprint gate the guard must reuse.
- `WL-0MSTLFW14000KPEC` — Exclude child items from audit-tier dispatch selection (completed). Root-only dispatch; uncovered children are flagged, never dispatched.
- `WL-0MUKE17XS0030LIC` — Document derived child-audit coverage in the global audit skill (open, low). Documentation follow-on, not a blocker.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No blocking clarifying questions were required — the seed context (including WL-0MUBVH8QG0020H9L's explicit assignment of uncovered-child reporting to this item and its derived-coverage decision) was sufficient to draft the brief. The genuinely open choices were design/implementation decisions, recorded above under **Design decisions & assumptions** (flag-vs-block, waiver storage, report scope, command naming) with rationale and repo evidence.

- Q: "Should the closure guard **block** or merely **flag** an unaudited completion?" — Decision (agent, pending producer confirmation): **flag** (non-fatal warning) plus a `wl doctor` report. Evidence: item title "flag + doctor report"; AC1 "flags or blocks"; WL-0MUBVH8QG0020H9L comment "WL-0MUBVH9FV0027COG … owns durable uncovered-child reporting". Source: `wl show WL-0MUBVH8QG0020H9L --children --json`; `src/commands/close.ts`.
- Q: "How is an explicit waiver represented?" — Decision (agent, pending producer confirmation): a durable, machine-readable waiver record surfaced via `wl show --json` (recommended `wl audit-waive`/`wl audit-unwaive`), not a parsed comment. Evidence: no waiver concept existed (`rg -ni waiver src/ packages/ docs/` → none); audit comments are deprecated/non-canonical; `src/migrations/index.ts` establishes the review-gated column precedent. Source: repo inspection.
- Q: "Does the report list stale audits too, or only missing audits?" — Decision (agent, pending producer confirmation): the report is scoped to **no audit record** (AC4 wording), coverage-aware; stale-but-present audits remain with the guard/icon surfaces. Evidence: AC4 "items with no audit"; problem statement "12 of 52 … have no audit record". Source: work-item description.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MSI8H3HP000K0RG** – Allow /skill:audit on complete/in_review items without a valid audit (completed)
- **WL-0MT32F90V008UAD2** – Downtime dispatch: use available slots while some slots busy (spare-capacity dispatch, default N instead of all-slots-free) (completed)
- **WL-0MTWU4XUD0001ALR** – Bot-created children must not silently demote completed/in_review parents (completed)

# Interview: LLM-Assisted Question Extraction

**Headline:** When `wl interview <id>` finds no parseable questions using the deterministic parser, optionally invoke a local LLM (via the existing embedding infrastructure) to extract unanswered questions from the description in free text.

## Problem Statement

The deterministic parser (`extractClarifyingSection` + `parseQAPairs`) requires an exact section header and rigid formatting. Real work items use varied formats (e.g., `## Appendix: Clarifying questions \& answers` with `- **Q1**: "..." — Answer (user@...): "..."). As a result, zero of the 17 `needsProducerReview=true` items are currently detectable. The original audit rejected WL-0MU55UDBJ008DJ67 stating: "The command does not reliably detect questions."

An LLM normaliser turns this hard format dependency into a soft one — it can extract questions regardless of prose format.

## Users

- **Producers** running `wl interview <id>` — they want the command to find questions even when the description doesn't follow the canonical format.
- **Developers** — they want the feature to work with local models (Ollama/Foundry), not require a cloud API key.

**User Story:** "As a producer running `wl interview`, I want the system to find questions even when they're written in natural prose, so I can answer them without manually searching the description."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When the deterministic parser finds no questions, and the `--llm` flag is set (or `intelligent: true` in config), the command calls a local LLM via the existing OpenAI-compatible embedding infrastructure `src/lib/search.ts`.
2. The LLM is asked to return a JSON array of `{ question: string }` objects extracted from the description, or an empty array if none found.
3. Each extracted question is presented to the user interactively (same `createPromptLoop` readline flow) for confirmation and answer.
4. Only confirmed questions are written to the description using the **deterministic re-serialiser** (`rebuildQAPairs` / `rebuildDescription`) — never written directly from LLM output.
5. When no LLM is available (no config, network failure, timeout), the command falls back to the existing deterministic-only message with no error.
6. The LLM call is bounded: description is truncated to 8 KB, a timeout of 15 seconds is enforced.
7. Tests cover: mock client returns valid questions, mock returns empty, mock throws error, no config available, timeout.

## Configuration

Opt-in via one of:
- `--llm` CLI flag: `wl interview <id> --llm`
- Config file: `intelligent: true` under `interview` section in `.worklog/config.yaml`

## Constraints

- No new dependencies — reuse `src/lib/search.ts` embedding infrastructure (OpenAI-compatible client, config resolution, graceful degradation).
- LLM is a *text completion* client, not an embedding client — but the same provider config, base URL, model, and auth apply. We should either:
  - (a) Add a `llm.*` config section parallel to `embedding.*`
  - (b) Or reuse the same provider config (the embedder already supports any OpenAI-compatible endpoint)
- The deterministic parser remains the primary path; LLM is strictly a fallback.
- Output is interactive-only (no --json mode for LLM calls).

## Key Files

- `src/commands/interview.ts` — New `--llm` option, LLM client invocation, user confirmation loop for extracted questions.
- `src/cli-types.ts` — Add `llm?: boolean` to `InterviewOptions`.
- `src/lib/search.ts` — Potentially add a `ChatClient` class alongside the existing `OpenAIEmbedder`, or reuse its config resolution for a completion client.
- `src/config.ts` — Add `interview.llm` or `llm.*` config schema.
- `tests/cli/interview.test.ts` — New test cases for LLM path.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Model availability:** Not all setups have an LLM configured. Fallback must be silent and graceful.
- **Cost:** One completion call per invocation (~2-3 KB input) is cheap even at $0.001/call, but should be bounded.
- **Hallucination:** The mandatory user-confirmation step before writing to the description mitigates this.
- **Scope creep risk:** Users may want batch extraction across multiple items or LLM-generated answers. Track separately.

## Goal

As a pi extension maintainer, I need the Worklog recovery extension to stop crashing the pi process when its captured `ExtensionContext` becomes stale after a session replacement/reload, so headless/audit pi runs are not aborted with a spurious `Connection error.`

## Problem

`packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/register-recovery.ts` captures the handler `ctx` in a module-level notify closure:

```ts
let _notifyFn: ((message: string, level: 'info' | 'warning' | 'error') => void) | null = null;
pi.on('agent_end', async (_event, ctx) => {
  _notifyFn = (message, level) => ctx.ui.notify(message, level);
});
pi.on('turn_end', async (_event, ctx) => {
  if (!_notifyFn) _notifyFn = (message, level) => ctx.ui.notify(message, level);
});
```

(and again around line ~212). `_notifyFn` is later invoked asynchronously from the recovery retry loop
(`_notifyRetryAttempt` → `_notifyFn`, called by `triggerInvisibleContinue`). After pi replaces or reloads the
session, `ctx.ui` throws:

```
Error: This extension ctx is stale after session replacement or reload. Do not use a captured pi or command ctx after ctx.newSession(), ctx.fork(), ctx.switchSession(), or ctx.reload(). ...
```

Because the call originates in a timer/async callback (`process.processTicksAndRejections`), pi does not catch it,
the Node process exits (stderr ends with the `Node.js v22.22.1` crash banner), and the calling consumer (e.g. the
SorraAgents audit runner) surfaces `provider_error: Connection error.`

## Evidence

- Stack trace: `at _notifyFn (register-recovery.ts:71:41)` → `at _notifyRetryAttempt (register-recovery.ts:549:5)` → `at triggerInvisibleContinue (register-recovery.ts:391:7)` → `at process.processTicksAndRejections`.
- Captured in SorraAgents audit debug log `~/.audit_debug/SorraAgents/audit_debug_SA-0MSRWAY9A005Q0CB.jsonl` (`context=parent`, `reason=provider_error`, `elapsed_seconds≈713`), and in every non-empty `raw_stderr` `provider_error` entry across that corpus.
- Originating SorraAgents item: **SA-0MUEIOGT2005IR7F** (this is the handoff requested there; the SorraAgents side will make its own `pi-client` extensions stale-ctx-safe and track its audit-runner change separately).

## Desired change

`_notifyFn` must never throw after the ctx is invalidated. Re-bind/re-capture the notify function from the
current handler ctx on each event (and/or guard the call), so a stale ctx results in the notification being
skipped rather than an uncaught exception. Do not change retry semantics otherwise.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The stale-ctx uncaught exception no longer occurs: the retry notification path (`_notifyRetryAttempt` → `_notifyFn`)
   never throws when the session ctx has been replaced/reloaded; the notification is skipped when the ctx is stale.
2. Regression test added: invoking the retry notification path with an invalidated/stale ctx asserts no throw.
3. The Worklog extension test suite passes with the change.
4. All related documentation and code comments are updated, including the recovery module header.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/register-recovery.ts` — `_notifyFn` capture and call sites.

## Related work

- SA-0MUEIOGT2005IR7F (SorraAgents) — corrected root-cause analysis and handoff.
- WL-0MQZX8BTN006N4BF — Automatically recover from appropriate server errors (parent retry-loop context).

# Downtime audits: prevent host-wide audit-slot / Local Proxy saturation from failing concurrent audits

**discovered-from:** SA-0MUG0WFP8008WN63 (SorraAgents worklog)

## Summary

On 2026-09-26 at least four downtime-dispatched audits were running concurrently on this
host, saturating both the shared Local Proxy and the audit runner's **host-wide** audit slot
(cheap-proxy mode forces `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY=1`). As a result the audit for
`SA-0MUG0WFP8008WN63` failed on **every** Pi call and was aborted with no verdict:

```
Audit concurrency limit reached: audit concurrency queue 'audit' saturated:
no slot within 90s (waited 90.1s, 1 item(s) in queue)
```

Supporting observations at the time:

- A direct Local Proxy generation request (`POST http://192.168.0.199:8000/v1/chat/completions`,
  model `plan`) returned no response within 180s, while `/v1/models` answered immediately.
- Host load average was ~70.
- Concurrent audits: `SA-0MUFM54CA0010LVD` (SorraAgents), `SA-0MTTSWHQE0072N9J` (SorraAgents),
  `CG-0MTW1EN0D003CSA0` (ContextHub) alongside the aborted `SA-0MUG0WFP8008WN63`.
- The failure degraded every acceptance criterion to `partial` on infrastructure evidence
  (not a code assessment), so the audit produced no usable verdict.

## Existing coverage that did not prevent this

- **Per-instance active-audit detection** (`WL-0MT47BQAT00375VB`, tests `WL-0MT47BMR7003ZQ66`):
  the audit tier is skipped when a non-stale `kind=audit` dispatch marker in
  `<cwd>/.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` maps to an item still `in_progress`.
- **Proxy-slot gating** already exists in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`
  (`slots_stale`, free-slot counts, local lease).

The observed concurrency spanned **multiple projects and possibly multiple herdr instances**,
and the audit runner's own host-wide semaphore/queue is a separate mechanism from the
dispatcher's per-project slot gate. The gap (per-instance vs host-wide coordination, and the
audit runner's 90s admission bound turning contention into an infra-partial verdict) is the
subject of this item.

## Desired change

1. **Host-wide audit serialisation (or deferral).** At most one audit-tier `/skill:audit` run
   should be actively executing per host — across herdr instances and projects — **or** the
   dispatcher must skip/defer audit dispatch while the audit runner's host-wide slot/queue is
   occupied or while the Local Proxy reports no free slots.
2. **Tolerate contention instead of failing.** When saturation is transient, the audit runner's
   admission wait should be sized so the run waits for a slot (`AUDIT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT`) and/or the
   dispatch is retried later, rather than aborting with an infra-partial verdict. An audit must
   not be reported as unavailable merely because other audits are legitimately running.
3. **Regression test.** With a simulated occupied host-wide audit slot (or two dispatcher
   instances on one host), a second audit is not started; the candidate falls through to the
   next tier or is deferred.
4. **Observability.** Log a clear skip/defer reason (e.g. `audit-host-saturated`) that includes
   the number of concurrent audits and the audit-runner queue/slot state.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Audit dispatch is serialised host-wide (single active audit run per host) **or** audit
      dispatch is skipped/deferred when the host-wide audit slot or Local Proxy slots are
      unavailable, including across projects and herdr instances.
- [ ] A regression test proves a second concurrent audit is not started while one is active
      (simulated occupied slot / second instance), and that the candidate is deferred or falls
      through to another tier.
- [ ] Contention produces a clear `audit-host-saturated` (or equivalent) skip/defer log line
      with the concurrent-audit count and queue/slot state.
- [ ] Documentation of the host-wide coordination contract and its relationship to the existing
      per-instance active-audit detection and proxy-slot gating.

  `~/.audit_debug/SorraAgents/audit_run_SA-0MUG0WFP8008WN63_20260926T175346.log`

# Create the `pane-triage` skill — gated close of idle panes in the current herdr workspace

## Goal

As a producer running several herdr workspaces, I want a `/skill:pane-triage`
that reports every pane in the invoking workspace, splits them into idle vs
active, surfaces each idle item's producer-review state and a log tail,
recommends the idle panes to close, and closes them **only after my explicit
approval** — so finished dispatch panes stop accumulating and holding memory/CPU.

## Context

- Agents that end with `</end_session>` leave their pane open; these accumulate
  and hold memory (see WL-0MUJL1NAH0042GOS).
- Existing auto-close work (WL-0MU308WSF0002JWN, WL-0MU4US5MP001JFEN) targets
  dispatch panes only and is already completed.
- This skill is the manual, workspace-scoped, approval-gated complement: it
  never closes anything unattended.

## Recommended source location

- **Canonical**: `SorraAgents/skill/pane-triage/` — `~/.pi/agent/skills` is a
  symlink to `SorraAgents/skill`, so a global skill must live there.
- Assumption: tracked in ContextHub because the herdr pane lifecycle work lives
  here. Confirm whether the skill should instead be ContextHub-local
  (`.pi/skills/pane-triage/`). If ContextHub-local, it will not be globally
  available.

## Skill specification (fixed defaults, no execution-control flags)

**Name / description**

- `name: pane-triage`
- `disable-model-invocation: true`
- description: "Triage and clean up panes in the current herdr workspace: idle
  vs active, producer-review state, log tails, then close idle panes after
  explicit producer approval."

**Scope and terminology**

- Workspace = `HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID` of the invoking pane (fallback
  `herdr pane current`); the report covers only this workspace.
- Tabs via `herdr tab list --workspace <id>`; panes via
  `herdr pane list --workspace <id>`.
- Idle = the pane's `agent_session.value` file exists and its last non-empty
  JSONL entry is an assistant message whose concatenated `text` blocks
  (`.rstrip()`) end with `</end_session>`.
- Active = any other pane (including plain shells with no session).
- Needs Review = the idle pane's work item has `needsProducerReview == true`
  (`wl show <id> --json`). Work-item id parsed from the trailing
  ` - <PREFIX>-<HASH>` in the pane label.

**Fixed defaults**

- Workspace: invoking workspace only; no cross-workspace roll-up.
- Log tail: 20 lines of the final session message per idle item (no active logs).
- Close recommendation: always emitted.
- Closing: enabled (dry-run off) but only after explicit approval.
- Output: markdown to stdout, pasted verbatim by the invoking agent.

**Algorithm**

1. Resolve workspace and fetch its label/number; error clearly if outside herdr.
2. Enumerate tabs and panes; index panes by tab.
3. Derive `title = label || terminal_title || "(untitled)"`.
4. Classify each pane idle/active; build the Idle and Active tables.
5. Enrich idle panes with work item id and `needsProducerReview` (`n/a` if no id).
6. Print each idle pane's final-message tail under the heading
   `<pane title> Needs Review <true|false>`.
7. Emit the report.
8. Emit the "Recommended to close" table.
9. Ask for producer approval, then close.

**Report structure**

```
# Pane report — <workspace label> (<workspace id>)

## Idle
| Tab | Title | Pane ID | Work item | Needs Review |

## Active
| Tab | Title | Pane ID |

## Idle item logs
### <pane title> Needs Review <true|false>
```text
<last 20 lines of final session message>
```

## Recommended to close
| Title | Pane ID | Work item | Needs Review | Reason |

## Closed
| Pane ID | Result |
```

**Recommend-to-close rules**

- Idle panes → recommended.
- Idle with `needsProducerReview == true` → recommended, annotated `review-pending`.
- Active panes / plain shells → not recommended.
- The invoking pane (`HERDR_PANE_ID`) → never recommended and never closed.

**Approval and closing**

- Mandatory blocking prompt: "N idle panes are recommended to close: <ids>.
  Close them? (yes / select / no)". `no`, or any ambiguity, closes nothing.
- `yes` → close all recommended; `select <ids>` → close only those.
- Immediately before closing, re-read `herdr pane list` and re-classify: drop
  any pane that is no longer idle, is the invoking pane, or no longer exists.
- Close with `herdr pane close <pane_id>`, one at a time; continue on individual
  failure and report a per-pane ledger; non-zero exit if any close failed.
- Idempotent: already-closed panes are skipped.

**Safety contract**

- Never close the invoking pane, under any circumstances.
- No approval → no mutation.
- Never act on the earlier snapshot alone; re-verify before closing.
- Never close more panes than approved.
- No unattended/automatic closing.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `/skill:pane-triage` resolves the invoking workspace from
   `HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID` (fallback `herdr pane current`) and reports only it.
2. Idle classification requires the last non-empty session entry to be an
   assistant message ending with `</end_session>`; a marker quoted mid-message
   does not qualify.
3. The report renders Idle and Active tables (tab, title, pane id) and, for idle
   items, the work item id and `needsProducerReview` value.
4. Each idle item's last 20 log lines are printed under the heading
   `<pane title> Needs Review <true|false>`.
5. A "Recommended to close" table lists idle panes and excludes the invoking
   pane; `needsProducerReview=true` rows are annotated `review-pending`.
6. No pane is closed without explicit producer approval (`yes`/`select`);
   `no`/ambiguity closes nothing; the invoking pane is never closed.
7. Approved panes are re-verified idle immediately before closing; any pane that
   became active is skipped with a reason in the Closed ledger.
8. Offline fixture tests cover classification, marker-mid-message rejection,
   work-item id parsing, `needsProducerReview` mapping, recommendation rules,
   and approval gating (no approval → zero close calls).

## References

- WL-0MUJL1NAH0042GOS — investigate why completed plan/intake sessions are not
  closed on completion (evaluated for deferral to this skill).
- WL-0MU308WSF0002JWN — log all dispatches and auto close all completed dispatch
  panes, except implement.
- WL-0MU4US5MP001JFEN — implement auto-close logic with implement exception.

## Goal
Author failing (TDD-first) unit tests for the new deterministic project→workspace resolver that maps a worklog root `R` to the herdr plugin (`label == "Work Items"`) pane/workspace for `R`, before the implementation item exists.

- Tests assert resolution matches on the plugin pane's logical project root read from `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD` (via `herdr pane process-info --pane <id>` + `/proc/<shell_pid>/environ`), and never on the pane's reported `cwd` (which is `<repo>/packages/herdr`) or the workspace label.

- Tests cover ambiguity (≥2 `Work Items` panes resolving to `R`): the resolver deterministically chooses the approved rule — prefer the focused matching pane, else the lowest pane id — and never selects a pane belonging to another root (AC3).
- Tests cover fail-closed `null` for malformed `herdr pane list` output, malformed `pane process-info` output, missing `/proc/<shell_pid>/environ`, missing `shell_pid`, and CLI non-zero exit — with raw output logged (AC3, AC7).
- Tests are written first and fail against the pre-implementation code.
- No production code is changed by this item.

## Minimal Implementation
- Extend `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.test.ts` (or add a focused `project-workspace.test.ts`) with fixtures for `herdr pane list` JSON (with/without `result` envelope, key-shape variants) and `pane process-info` JSON, plus injected deps stubs for the `/proc` env read.
- Reuse the existing fail-closed parser conventions from `dispatcher-anchor.ts`.
- Keep tests hermetic — no live herdr invocation.

- Automated downtime dispatch scope only; do not change manual flows.
- Follow `packages/herdr` existing test style/framework (vitest).
- Do not delete existing per-prefix tests here — that belongs to the implementation item that retires them.

## Risky assumptions
- Plugin panes are identifiable by `label == "Work Items"` and expose `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD` + `HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID` in the shell process environment (verified live on this host).

## Deliverables
- New/updated test file(s) with the coverage above.

- Test-first: none (blocks the project-workspace resolver implementation item).
